title: Freeze did not bind analytics, tiers, calendar, or data layer
description: research_freeze_v1 fingerprinted only strategy/portfolio/engine/ranking modules. metrics.py, validation.py (bootstrap/DSR/walk-forward), tiers.py, calendar.py, experiments.py, holdout.py, tax.py and the entire data layer (loader, importer, quality gate, security master, providers) could be edited after freezing without detection — every reported number, evidence tier, and gate decision was alterable post-freeze.
reproduction: audit probe 1: diff aitb.freeze._FROZEN_MODULES against behavior-defining modules
expected: any code that computes, tiers, gates or records a result is fingerprint-bound
impact: convincing but unfrozen results possible; freeze guarantee vacuous for analytics
invalidates_prior_results: no real results existed under v1; synthetic demos regenerated

title: Freeze verified only at experiment time, not at analysis/report time
description: run_robustness, run_capacity, run_company_analysis, make_report ran real mode without verify_freeze(). Rankings, robustness statistics, capacity estimates and the report itself could be produced by modified code after the experiments ran under the frozen code.
reproduction: audit probe 2: grep verify_freeze in real-mode scripts
expected: every real-mode entry point verifies the freeze
impact: derived analytics and the decision surface were unfrozen
fix: verify_freeze() added to all real-mode scripts

title: Holdout lock not tamper-evident: deleting the file restored clean status
description: holdout_lock.json was the only record; _load() returned a pristine state when the file was missing, so rm holdout_lock.json silently erased a compromised flag and the entire access log.
reproduction: audit probe 3: record two accesses (compromised=True), delete file, holdout_status shows compromised=False, 0 accesses
expected: append-only, tamper-evident; a compromised holdout stays compromised
impact: holdout discipline unenforceable against a single file deletion
fix: every freeze/access event is hash-chained and mirrored into the append-only experiment registry; holdout_status cross-checks lock vs registry and forces compromised on mismatch; events bind freeze hash + store fingerprint

title: Missing capacity estimate treated as passing (fail-open)
description: The advancement check `(not len(crow)) or capacity >= 1e6` passed whenever a strategy had NO row in capacity.csv — an absent estimate counted as adequate capacity.
reproduction: audit probe 4: source inspection + logic table
impact: a strategy could advance to paper-trade without any capacity evidence
fix: fail-closed: capacity must be present, finite and >= $1M; NaN/inf metric values also block via _finite()

title: Compromised holdout and failed/stale quality gate did not block advancement
description: The brief displayed a compromised-holdout banner but still computed survivors; it also never re-checked the gate status or whether the store fingerprint still matched the gate (results could be stale).
expected: compromised holdout, non-passing gate, or fingerprint mismatch force DO NOTHING
impact: invalid evidence could produce a PAPER-TRADE recommendation
fix: blocked_reason preconditions force DO NOTHING and empty the survivor list

title: CAGR annualized by row-count/252 instead of elapsed calendar time
description: cagr() used len(returns)/252 as 'years'. On the synthetic business-day calendar (~261 rows/yr) this overstated elapsed years and understated CAGR by ~35-40bp/yr (probe: true 10.00% reported as 9.63%). On the NYSE calendar (~250-253 sessions/yr) the error is small but nonzero.
reproduction: audit probe 6: 4-calendar-year b-day series with known 10% CAGR
impact: all CAGR/Calmar figures biased; cross-calendar comparisons inconsistent
fix: elapsed (index[-1]-index[0]).days/365.25 when a DatetimeIndex is present
invalidates_prior_results: synthetic demo artifacts regenerated; no real results existed

title: Experiment records carried no data-store fingerprint
description: Real-mode experiment records contained only a universe hash — no binding to the validated store contents or governing freeze, so the lineage chain raw->checksum->import->store->run->record->report was broken at the store->record link, and a report could silently present results from a superseded store.
expected: records bind store fingerprint + freeze hash; report invalidated on mismatch
impact: stale or substituted data undetectable downstream
fix: records embed lineage {store_fingerprint, freeze_hash} in real mode; report gains a provenance section that flags fingerprint mismatches as STALE and lists artifact hashes

title: Deflated-Sharpe trial battery excluded failed variants
description: run_robustness built trial_sharpes only from OK runs; errored variants (still trials) were dropped, understating N and making the DSR correction too lenient.
expected: every attempted variant counts as a trial
fix: failed variants enter the battery as zero-Sharpe trials

title: Tier assignment failed open: unknown/missing family promoted to Tier A
description: assign_tier fell through to Tier A for any record whose family was missing or unrecognized — omitted metadata produced the HIGHEST evidence tier.
expected: missing tier metadata can never promote
impact: misclassified evidence could reach the Tier A leaderboard and the brief's tier_A check
fix: unknown family -> Tier B with explicit reason; missing status -> Tier C; dead 'or True' flag logic removed

title: Verdict layer alone admits ~3% of pure-noise strategies
description: 30 random-return strategies against a noise benchmark: 1 achieved robust_candidate through the composite-score + relative-hurdle verdict (probe 7). The verdict layer is not the last line of defense — advancement additionally requires Tier A, bootstrap CI excluding zero, concentration and capacity checks — but the verdict label itself has a nonzero false-discovery rate.
expected: near-zero false discovery at the final decision layer (achieved via stacked criteria)
impact: verdict labels in reports should be read as candidates, not conclusions
fix: not fixed by design: tightening the frozen ranking criteria mid-audit would itself be a spec change; the layered advancement criteria are the control; documented in report

title: No per-bar accounting invariant existed
description: The engine had endpoint tests but no continuous invariant tying equity changes to P&L + interest - costs each bar, so a future accounting regression could pass endpoint tests while leaking value mid-path.
reproduction: absence; hand-ledger probes 8a-c all reconciled exactly (no active defect found)
expected: audit mode asserts dEquity == overnight P&L + intraday P&L + interest - costs on every bar
impact: latent-regression risk, not an active error (hand ledgers reconciled to the cent)
fix: check_invariants flag / AITB_ENGINE_INVARIANTS=1 enables the per-bar invariant with 1e-6 relative tolerance

title: Dividends modeled as continuous reinvestment, not cash ledger entries
description: Ratio-adjusted (total-return-consistent) prices embed dividends in the price path; there is no discrete cash dividend credit. Internally consistent and benchmark-consistent, but it assumes frictionless same-security reinvestment and the tax overlay estimates dividend income from a configured yield rather than actual distributions.
impact: small overstatement of compounding for dividend payers vs a cash-account investor; tax dividend estimate approximate
fix: documented in README and report methodology; discrete dividend ledger listed as future work

title: Freeze does not bind dependency versions or in-process monkey-patching
description: pip freeze is recorded in the run fingerprint but not enforced; a different pandas/numpy could alter numerics. In-process monkey-patching after verification is unpreventable in Python. Both are recorded (fingerprint) rather than enforced.
impact: reproducibility depends on honoring the recorded environment
fix: documented; strict pin-file enforcement listed as future work

title: Dead logic in gate_flags (macro_revised '... or True')
description: The macro_revised flag was computed then overridden by 'or True' — harmless (FRED is always revised) but misleading.
fix: replaced with explicit constant True + comment

title: Composite score includes holdout Sharpe by design
description: The ranking's 2x holdout-Sharpe term means the final ordering uses holdout results. This is the sanctioned single final evaluation (spec frozen before any real holdout view, one logged access), not selection leakage — but it must never be described as out-of-sample model selection, and re-running ranking repeatedly against holdout data would erode its validity (now mitigated by the tamper-evident access log and the compromised flag blocking advancement).
actual: as designed; reports label holdout columns
fix: documented in audit report and methodology

title: Experiment ID omitted the universe, so an expanded roster reused old results
description: experiment_id() hashed (spec, provider, data_mode, scenario, data_span) but NOT the investable universe. run_experiment skips any ID already in the registry and reloads its stored equity curve, so re-running an unchanged strategy against an EXPANDED universe returned the previous universe's results while recording them as current. The defect could not fire inside a single freeze, because the freeze holds the universe fixed — it fires precisely at a freeze boundary that widens the roster, which is exactly when old and new numbers are most likely to be compared.
reproduction: expand configs/universe.yaml; re-run scripts/run_experiments.py; every pre-existing variant is skipped as cached despite a different investable set
expected: a run against a different universe is a different experiment with a different ID
actual: identical ID; cached curve from the narrower universe reused and presented as the new result
impact: silently stale results at every universe expansion; cross-universe contamination of every downstream ranking, scorecard and report
fix: experiment_id() now binds universe_hash (tickers plus listing windows) and freeze_version; records carry universe_hash and universe_size; ranking.current_cohort() and platform.catalog.current_registry() restrict every leaderboard, scorecard and comparison to one universe cohort; superseded cohorts are retained and labelled, never deleted
invalidates_prior_results: no real results existed under v1 or v2; the synthetic v2 cohort is retained in the registry and excluded from all comparisons by universe hash

title: Append-only registry has no uniqueness guard on experiment IDs
description: ExperimentRegistry.append() writes unconditionally. Two runner processes started against the same registry both pass the existing_ids() check (read once at entry) and then both append records for the same IDs. Observed during the freeze-v3 run when a background launch was mistakenly issued twice: 718 records were written where 359 were expected, every ID duplicated, and concurrent parquet writes to the same curve path are not atomic either. Values were identical because the pipeline is deterministic, so no number was wrong — but headline counts double and curve files are potentially torn. RECURRED on the first real-data study (2026-08-05): three overlapping runs — the run_first_real_study.sh invocation plus two manual pipeline chains — wrote 1,644 records for 646 experiments, a 2.5x inflation of every count. All duplicates agreed exactly on every metric, so no reported number was wrong, but the concurrent store access also tripped the gate's fingerprint check and blocked make_report and run_company_analysis.
reproduction: start scripts/run_experiments.py twice concurrently against one registry root; inspect duplicate IDs in results/<mode>/experiments.jsonl
expected: a second append of an existing ID is refused, or the runner refuses to start while another holds the registry
actual: both processes append; duplicates are only removed at display time
impact: inflated run counts and torn curve files; no incorrect metric, because runs are deterministic
fix: scripts/run_experiments.py takes an O_EXCL lock on the registry root (.runner.lock) and exits with an explanatory message if another runner holds it. Deliberately NOT fixed inside ExperimentRegistry.append(): experiments.py is bound by the research freeze, and changing it would supersede the freeze the first real study ran under, forcing a full re-run to fix a bookkeeping defect. The lock removes the only way the condition arises. The real registry was de-duplicated (first write wins; all copies byte-equal on metrics) and tests/test_audit_regressions.py::test_registry_has_no_duplicate_ids covers both registries.
invalidates_prior_results: no — duplicates were exact copies, so every metric, ranking and verdict is unchanged; only record COUNTS were inflated, and the registry has been de-duplicated in place

title: Strategy family labelled by source file, not by construction
description: Five long-only screens (GrossProfitability, ResearchIntensity, AccrualQuality, PostEarningsDrift, DispersionTimedSelection) were assigned family='longshort' because they were authored in longshort.py. `family` is part of strategy.spec() and therefore of the experiment ID; it also groups the deflated-Sharpe trial batteries in run_robustness.py and drives the correlation-by-family chart on the site. The mislabelling made the site state that hedged strategies show a median correlation of 0.83 to the index — the exact opposite of the finding — because five long-only members dragged the family median up. The genuinely hedged strategies measure about zero (market-neutral book: -0.005 monthly correlation to QQQ across all cost scenarios).
reproduction: compare each class's `family` attribute against whether its build() can emit a negative weight; render _independence_section and read the family median
expected: family describes the construction; only strategies able to hold a negative position are 'longshort'
actual: family described the source file; the site's central conclusion was inverted
impact: site published a false headline conclusion; deflated-Sharpe trial batteries grouped unrelated strategies together, and after the correction the same strategies briefly appeared under two family labels, splitting their batteries and overstating significance on both sides
fix: families reassigned to longshort / quality / factor; experiments.yaml split into longshort, quality and meta_timing groups; freeze v4 reissued (hash 384dc48714fc530de3f3a4a9168df12f) before any real-data run; 36 superseded synthetic records whose recorded family contradicted the class definition were removed from the registry.
invalidates_prior_results: no real results existed under v4; the affected synthetic records were removed and the grid re-run. The v3 real study is unaffected — the longshort family did not exist under v3.
